misconceptions.description: Assuming adult learners want total freedom with no design guidance
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that adult learning should remove structure entirely
misconceptions.feedback: Adults value autonomy, but strong adult learning still needs structure, relevance, and clear performance pathways.

misconceptions.description: Treating prior experience as automatically accurate and helpful
misconceptions.trigger: learner ignores the possibility that adults also bring misconceptions or outdated habits
misconceptions.feedback: Prior experience is valuable, but it can also carry biases and misconceptions. Good design surfaces and works with that experience rather than assuming it is all correct.

misconceptions.description: Assuming adults only want practical tips and never need conceptual framing
misconceptions.trigger: learner removes explanatory models entirely in favor of only immediate tips
misconceptions.feedback: Adults often want practical relevance, but theory still matters when it helps them make better decisions in new situations.
